headline: Onboard subject to conditions: the business verifies from its own web presence and its financial record clears once the filings are read, leaving the adverse media source as the only unread finding and two documents to collect.

body.text: Read as filings rather than counts, this file is in better shape than its totals suggest — eight of ten liens closed, nine of ten litigations another company's business in a Georgia circuit court, and the tenth a foreclosure naming fifteen defendants. What is actually outstanding is three things of three kinds. One is a finding nobody has read: the high risk adverse media source, now the only item on the file carrying a score without an article behind it. One is a document only the customer can supply: a Certificate of Good Standing, because the state of formation publishes no status here. One is a policy decision the bank makes about itself, not about this business — whether business-verification software sold to regulated institutions sits inside the accepted-industry list. The two open UCC filings warrant a question to the secured parties rather than a condition, since neither states a sum and one names an unrelated co-debtor.

followUps.text: Pull the adverse media source and read it, since it is the only finding on the file carrying a risk score with nothing behind it.
Ask the two secured parties on the open UCC filings what they secure and for how much, and confirm the Virginia filing is not a debtor-name collision given the secured party's line of work.
Request a Certificate of Good Standing for the state of formation from the customer, which is the only evidence of standing available because the state publishes none.
Take a beneficial-ownership certification and screen every owner it names against watchlists and PEP lists, since the clearance so far covers only the individuals the applicant submitted.
Decide whether business-verification software sold to regulated institutions sits inside the accepted-industry policy — a judgement about the bank's own appetite, not about this record.
Take the customer's stated expected activity — volumes, counterparties and payment types — since nothing in the record reaches it.
Order the people-level lien, litigation, bankruptcy and criminal checks, which are defined and returned nothing on this pull.
Ask the customer why the submitted individual is not named on the company's own site when the state filings list them as an officer, and re-run the web phone check.
